_comment: Registered council-attendance metrics (road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-b Phase 1.4). Registered in the same change that ships the instrument (quorum_result, events_log schema v2) and BEFORE any of the three outcomes the quorum-solo-floor blocker chooses between — a threshold picked after seeing the rate is a threshold fitted to the rate. Every number below is pre-registered, not measured; the honest-gap field on each metric says so in its own words. Changing one is a PR citing evidence, never a drive-by edit.

instrument.emitter: src/scripts/ai_council/events_log.ts::appendQuorumEvent, called from the two evaluateQuorum sites in src/scripts/council_cli.ts (construction and post_run stages)
instrument.fields: status, threshold, total, present, solo_concluded, stage, absent[{member, reason}]
instrument.privacy: absent entries carry a member name and a closed-union reason token only — QuorumAbsentEntry has no field able to hold free-form text, so the raw provider error string both call sites hold alongside it cannot reach the log. Exclusion by construction, not by scrubbing.
instrument.double_counting: one pass emits up to TWO lines (stage=construction, stage=post_run). Any rate below is computed over ONE stage, never both summed — post_run where a pass ran to completion, construction where it did not.

attendance_rate.definition: present / total per pass, over stage='post_run' lines. The share of configured members that actually produced a usable response.

threshold._investigate: a median attendance below 0.75 over the review window means the configured roster is not the roster that runs, and the config is describing a council that does not convene. Advisory — nothing gates on it.

attendance_rate.honest_gap: There is no baseline. No quorum event existed before this change, so 0.75 is a pre-registered decision boundary and NOT a measured p50 or p90. The first report run establishes the baseline; if it lands far from 0.75 in either direction, the number moves by evidence in a PR and the original registration stays visible in git history.

solo_conclusion_rate.definition: share of concluded passes where exactly one member was present (quorum.ts::isSoloConcluded), over stage='post_run' lines. The degradation reading filters total > 1; the unfiltered rate includes structurally-solo n=1 councils. Both are recoverable because the record carries total.

threshold._null: the quorum-solo-floor blocker's own pre-registration: a rate under 5% over the review window IS the null, and publishing it closes step 1.5 without adding a third member or a min_present floor. Above 5%, the blocker picks between its other two outcomes (a third CLI member, or gate-scoped min_present: 2).

solo_conclusion_rate.honest_gap: 5% is the blocker's committed decision boundary, chosen before any pass was measured. It is a boundary, not a prediction. Note also what this rate CANNOT distinguish: a member absent because the operator never installed its binary (structural, expected) from one absent because a live call timed out (a real degradation). The absent_reason_distribution below is what separates them, which is why all three metrics are registered together and none of them is sufficient alone.

absent_reason_distribution.definition: counts per reason token across absent[] entries, over both stages, reported separately per stage. Tokens: no_binary, no_auth, timeout, quota (AbsentReason, transport_resolver.ts) plus the runtime fallbacks unavailable and binary_missing.

threshold._unclassified: 'unavailable' is the fallback written when absentReasonFromCliFailure cannot classify a failure. A sustained share above 10% means the classifier has a blind spot and the taxonomy needs a token, not that the councils are unhealthy — this ceiling measures the INSTRUMENT, deliberately, so the other two metrics cannot quietly rest on unclassified data.

absent_reason_distribution.honest_gap: The six tokens are the vocabulary the tree writes today. If a real distribution shows one token absorbing nearly everything, that is a finding about the classifier and not a threshold breach. No target distribution is registered, because there is no shape a healthy one is known to have.

honest_null_consequence: If the review window shows a solo-conclusion rate under 5%, the null is published with the same prominence a finding would get and step 1.5 closes against it — no third member, no min_present floor, no mechanism added to solve a problem the data says is not there. If attendance telemetry accumulates and nobody reads it by review_by, that is the fossilization failure this file's siblings name: the report is the re-verification procedure, and an unread instrument is a dead one.
report_command: grep '"action":"quorum_result"' agents/runtime/council/events.log — no dedicated report script ships with the instrument, on purpose: one jq-able line format is cheaper than a reporter nobody runs, and a reporter written before any data exists would be fitted to imagined data.
